name: pregnancy through drinking, eating

attributes.attribute: goddess or heroine made pregnant through the mouth
often from drinking a worm or insect in water or wine

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Pregnancy through drinking or eating is a mythic motif. In several Celtic myths a goddess or heroine becomes pregnant through the mouth. The cause is eating or drinking. Most often the pregnancy results from drinking down a worm or other insect drowned in water or wine. In one tale the divine beauty Étain became a fly and drowned in a cup of wine. A princess drank it, and nine months later Étain was reborn in a new and beautiful form. The hero Concobar mac Nessa was born clutching a worm. His mother Nessa wished to prove his father was a worm she drank. The motif appears in other cultures. Chinese emperors were said to be born after their mothers ate or drank something unusual.

okr.objective: Explain the mythic motif of pregnancy brought on by drinking or eating.
key_results: States the motif that pregnancy results from drinking or eating
Gives the Étain and Conchobar examples
